title: Economics elevator tests and competitive notes
summary: Working doc for short-form elevator pitches, claim testing matrix, and competitive rebuttals focused on latency + token unit cost. Purpose: rapid experiments with SDRs and Solutions engineers to identify 2–3 crisp claims that map to measurable customer outcomes.
audience: SDRs, AE playingbook writers, product marketing, solutions engineering
goals: Identify 3 validated claims (speed, cost per 1k tokens, predictable tail latency)
Create 6 short elevator lines for outreach and demos
Define a lightweight A/B evidence test plan for field reps
key_claims: Average token cost reductions of 20–50% via automatic batching + prefix caching compared to naive cloud endpoints
Consistent p95 tail latency suitable for interactive UIs: typical p95 100–200ms for short-chat flows (vs competitor p95 often >>300ms in our tests)
Seamless downgrade/fallback policy that keeps user-facing features online during peak load (fewer customer errors and session drops)
Transparent unit economics (token-level breakdowns) so teams can model cost at feature scale
proof_points: Benchmarks run Jan 2025: 10k synthetic chat sessions, avg token size 24, Redwood inference engine with KV caching reduced token compute by 36% vs baseline naive batching on competitor infra (GPX cloud). See linked_artifact confluence:INF-5678 for raw results
Field pilot: SaaS search team (pilot) showed 27% lower per-query cost after enablement of continuous batching and 15% lower average latency for query-first flows over two weeks
SRE incident history: automated fallback prevented outage in a Dedicated pool during region interruption — customer observed graceful degradation (latency rose but error rate stayed <0.5%)
Observable cost dashboard: token breakdowns surfaced a heavy DEBUG prompt that, once trimmed, reduced monthly spend forecast by 18% for one customer
competitive_observations: Competitor A emphasizes model freshness and large-model access but publishes few concrete latency percentiles — in customer tests they prioritized throughput over tail latency and often expose higher p95s

Competitor B promotes aggressive quantization to claim cost savings; however, quality regressions are visible on instruction-following prompts we run (measurable drop in ROUGE/accuracy on internal evals)
Self-hosted runtime vendors tout cost parity but ignore operational burden: long lead times for upgrades, brittle kernel compatibility across GPUs — a blocker for platform engineering teams
Some cloud vendors offer autoscale but lack predictable p95 SLOs for interactive apps; their burst queues create noisy neighbors that inflate tail latency
risks_and_mitigations: Claim: 20–50% cost reduction. Risk: variability by workload. Mitigation: always qualify claim with a workload profile and offer an on-site quick eval; lead with range and an example workload

Claim: p95 100–200ms. Risk: dependent on model size and sequence length. Mitigation: provide explicit limits (e.g., for <512 tokens, 7B-class instruction models) and include fallbacks for longer sequences

Competitive attack: quality-first vendors say our cost claims compromise output quality. Mitigation: publish eval slices where quantization + caching maintain quality (examples and diff snippets) and offer demo workloads
Operational objection: 'we can't trust hosted numbers' — Mitigation: enable a short private trial/Dedicated pilot and provide telemetry export to customer observability stack
sales_snippets: Hook (30s): 'We help teams get production-grade LLM features online with predictable cost and latency — typically 20–40% lower token spend and half the p95 latency you see from generic endpoints.'
Demo opener: 'For interactive chat use-cases we target p95 under 200ms by combining smart prefix caching and continuous batching — we can show you a side-by-side in 10 minutes.'

Objection handle (quality vs cost): 'We don't trade away quality — our optimizer suggests quantization profiles per workload and we run evals to ensure no output regressions before recommending changes.'
Value metric close: 'If you ship 10M tokens/month, a 25% unit cost cut is $X/mo — we can model it in 15 minutes with your telemetry.'
experiment_plan: Step 1: Create 3 outreach variants using the sales_snippets above (A: speed-first, B: cost-first, C: predictable-SLA-first)
Step 2: Run 2-week SDR experiment (50 reps, 100 target accounts each, track meetings and demo requests)
Step 3: For accounts that accept demo, run side-by-side demo using our evaluation harness vs top competitor and capture p50/p95 and token cost delta
Step 4: Collect qualitative feedback from SEs about which claim closed or advanced the deal and tag reasons in CRM
Step 5: Iterate copy based on conversion lift and push winners into playbook
metrics_to_track: SDR conversion rate by variant (open -> meeting)
Demo to PO (proof-of-concept) conversion within 30 days
Average token cost delta in demo (percent and $)
Measured p95 latency delta in live demo
Time to first value for pilot (days)
notes: Working notes: prioritize customers with interactive UIs (search, chat, collaborative editors). Avoid blanket percent statements in external content — always include ranges and workload qualifiers. Next steps: align with SEs to instrument demo harness for quick injection of customer prompts. Follow up with Priya for updated benchmark CSVs and with Carlos for field rep training schedule.
